title: Download & Install
lede: Flash a ready-made image, or download the release for your platform and run the install steps. Then add only the optional components for the features you want; Polaris detects what is installed at runtime and hides the UI for anything missing.

requirements.title: System requirements
requirements.sub: The main limiting factor is RAM. Everything else is comfortable on a modern SBC, and the recommended board adds GPU and NPU acceleration.
requirements.ramNote: Polaris uses 0.7 to 1.7 GB of RAM on average, so 2 GB is the practical floor. A Raspberry Pi 4 with 2 GB still runs the app, with client-side WASM offloading the heavy live-stack math.
requirements.recommendedNote: Recommended board: the Orange Pi 5 Pro with 4 GB or more. It runs the whole app end to end, with OpenCL acceleration on the GPU and GraXpert AI on the NPU. More boards are on the test bench: two Orange Pi 4 Pro (4 GB), a Celeron PC stick, and a Radxa Dragon Q6A (expected to be the most powerful of the lot).

rows.notes: Broadcom BCM2837 (4x Cortex-A53, up to 1.2 GHz), VideoCore IV GPU. Runs, but tight; PHD2 GUI embed is auto-disabled (32-bit ARM gate).
Broadcom BCM2711 (4x Cortex-A72, up to 1.8 GHz), VideoCore VI GPU, LPDDR4. The RAM floor: 2 GB is the minimum to run; client-side WASM offloads the heavy math.
Broadcom BCM2712 (4x Cortex-A76, up to 2.4 GHz), VideoCore VII GPU, LPDDR4X. Lossless: live stacking plus simultaneous Studio jobs are fine.

Two units incoming. Allwinner A733 (2x Cortex-A76 + 6x Cortex-A55, up to 2.0 GHz), Imagination BXM-4-64 GPU, 3 TOPS NPU, LPDDR5. Same GPU-plus-NPU story as the 5 Pro: OpenCL on the GPU and GraXpert on the NPU, pending validation.
Proven daily driver. RK3588S (4x Cortex-A76 + 4x Cortex-A55), Mali-G610 GPU, 6 TOPS NPU. Full experience: OpenCL on the GPU and GraXpert AI on the NPU.

Qualcomm QCS6490 (octa-core Kryo: 1x 2.7 GHz + 3x 2.4 GHz + 4x 1.9 GHz), Adreno 643 GPU (OpenCL), Hexagon NPU up to 12 TOPS, LPDDR5. Incoming, expected to be the most powerful board tested so far, pending validation.
Intel Celeron J4105 (4 cores, up to 2.5 GHz), Intel UHD 600 GPU (OpenCL), 8 GB LPDDR4, 128 GB eMMC, Gigabit LAN. Ships with Windows 11 Pro. Incoming, results to follow.
Same feature set as Linux, plus vendor DSLR drivers.

images.title: Ready-to-flash images
images.sub: The fastest way to get going: each image is a Linux OS with Polaris preinstalled and configured for that board. Flash it to an SD card (or USB / eMMC), boot, and open the browser. Use Raspberry Pi Imager, balenaEtcher, or Rufus. Images live on Google Drive and are added as each board is validated.
images.bootNote: On boot, the image starts Polaris automatically and it is ready to use, no setup needed. If the device cannot join a known WiFi network and it has WiFi, it raises its own hotspot named Polaris-Hotspot (password polaris1234). Connect to that, then open the Polaris UI in your browser.

items.note: x86 board: flash to USB or write to the internal eMMC, not an SD card.

update.title: Updating Polaris on a flashed image
update.intro: Already running a flashed image? SSH in (user polaris, password polaris), download the latest .deb, and install it over the running version. Your profiles and data are kept.
update.code:
ssh polaris@<ip-or-hostname>
wget https://github.com/DanWBR/NINA.Polaris/releases/latest/download/polaris_arm64.deb
sudo dpkg -i polaris_arm64.deb
update.note: Use polaris_arm64.deb for ARM SBCs (Raspberry Pi, Orange Pi); pick the package that matches your board otherwise. Change the default polaris password after first login.

download.title: Download
download.sub: Grab the server build for the machine that runs your rig, then follow the install steps below. Prefer zero setup? Use a ready-to-flash image above.

groups.name: Server (runs on the rig)
groups.note: Install on the Raspberry Pi, SBC, or mini PC that controls your gear.

groups.name: Client apps (connect from a device)
groups.note: Optional native app to reach the server. Any browser also works, so no app is required.

tldr.title: Bare minimum to boot
tldr.note: That is all the home page needs. Every other feature has its own dependency, listed under optional components below.

rows.label: Runtime
rows.windows: .NET 10 Desktop Runtime (bundled in the self-contained build)
rows.linux: .NET 10 Runtime, or use the self-contained build

platformsSection.title: Install
platformsSection.sub: Step by step for each platform once you have the files. The published builds are self-contained, so there is no separate runtime to install.

platforms.name: Raspberry Pi 4 / 5
platforms.summary: The recommended path. The .deb creates the user, a systemd unit, the indi-web venv, apt dependencies, and a self-signed HTTPS cert.
platforms.notes: Running at https://<hostname>.local:5000 in about 30 seconds. Manage it with: sudo systemctl status polaris, sudo journalctl -u polaris -f, sudo systemctl restart polaris.

platforms.name: Other Linux (portable)
platforms.summary: For Fedora, Arch, or any non-Debian distro, or when you prefer no systemd integration. Replace linux-arm64 with linux-x64 for Intel/AMD.
platforms.notes: Runs in the foreground. Wire your own service unit if you want it to survive reboots.

platforms.name: Windows mini PC
platforms.summary: Portable, no installer. ARM64 build also available (polaris-win-arm64.zip) for Surface Pro X and some Copilot+ PCs.
platforms.steps:
Invoke-WebRequest -Uri "https://github.com/DanWBR/NINA.Polaris/releases/latest/download/polaris-win-x64.zip" -OutFile polaris.zip
Expand-Archive polaris.zip
cd polaris-win-x64
.\NINA.Polaris.exe
platforms.notes: Open https://localhost:5000 and accept the self-signed cert once. Remember to open the firewall (see below).

platforms.name: Docker
platforms.summary: Multi-arch image (arm64 + amd64). The compose file in the repo includes indiserver in the same stack.
platforms.notes: Volumes mount /config (profiles) and /images (FITS output). On Linux use --network host, or port-forward TCP 5000 and UDP 5353 in compose.

platforms.name: Build from source
platforms.summary: For developers or unsupported platforms. Needs the .NET 10 SDK and Git (with submodules).
platforms.steps:
git clone https://github.com/DanWBR/NINA.Polaris.git
cd NINA.Polaris
./deploy/publish-linux-arm64.sh   # or publish-linux-x64.sh / publish-win-x64.ps1
./publish/linux-arm64/NINA.Polaris
platforms.notes: Build and test target net10.0. The stellarium-web submodule ships pinned .js/.wasm, so Emscripten is only needed if you bump the engine.

firewall.title: Open the firewall
firewall.sub: Polaris listens on TCP 5000 (HTTP) and UDP 5353 (mDNS, so <hostname>.local resolves). Both are blocked by default.
firewall.windows:
New-NetFirewallRule -DisplayName "N.I.N.A. Polaris" -Direction Inbound -Protocol TCP -LocalPort 5000 -Action Allow -Profile Private,Domain
New-NetFirewallRule -DisplayName "mDNS (Polaris)" -Direction Inbound -Protocol UDP -LocalPort 5353 -Action Allow -Profile Private,Domain
firewall.linux:
sudo ufw allow 5000/tcp
sudo ufw allow 5353/udp
firewall.note: On Linux without ufw: iptables -A INPUT -p tcp --dport 5000 -j ACCEPT. The .deb install handles this for you.

optionalSection.title: Optional components
optionalSection.sub: Add only what you need. Polaris lights up each feature when its tool is present and degrades gracefully when it is not.

optionalGroups.name: Equipment drivers
optionalGroups.intro: At least one bus is required to control hardware. Both can coexist; the active rig stores a per-device driver choice.

items.name: INDI
items.purpose: Preferred on Linux. The indi-full meta-package ships the daemon plus 100+ drivers (ZWO, Canon, EQMod, Celestron, weather, ...).
items.windows: Runs via WSL2 or a windi build; most Windows users pick Alpaca instead.

items.name: ASCOM / Alpaca
items.purpose: Preferred on Windows. Polaris discovers Alpaca devices over the LAN via UDP.
items.windows: ASCOM Platform 7+ (free) + the driver pack per device. Alpaca on by default.
items.linux: Run an Alpaca-compatible device server; most modern drivers expose Alpaca natively.

items.name: Vendor SDKs (DSLR / mirrorless)
items.purpose: Canon, Nikon, and Sony DSLR/mirrorless on Windows. Drop the DLLs into plugins/ after registering with the vendor (EULA blocks redistribution).
items.windows: Canon EDSDK 13.x+ in plugins/canon-edsdk/, Nikon SDK in plugins/nikon-sdk/, Sony SDK in plugins/sony-sdk/.
items.linux: Not needed: DSLRs use indi_gphoto_ccd from indi-full.

optionalGroups.name: Plate solving
optionalGroups.intro: Required for Slew & Center (the centering loop). Without any solver, Slew Only still slews the mount. Polaris dispatches primary then blind fallback across whatever is installed.

items.name: ASTAP
items.purpose: Default solver. Fast (about 1 to 3 s), works offline, MIT. Recommended for everyone.
items.windows: astap.exe installer + the H17/H18 star database (~2 GB).

items.name: PlateSolve3
items.purpose: Faster than ASTAP at long focal lengths. Free for non-commercial use.

items.name: Astrometry.net (local)
items.purpose: The gold standard, but slow on a Pi (about 30 to 60 s).
items.linux: sudo apt install astrometry.net + index files.

items.name: Astrometry.net (online)
items.purpose: Last resort. About 30 to 60 s per solve, free with an API key.

optionalGroups.name: Autoguiding
optionalGroups.intro: Polaris guides out of the box with a built-in, native PHD2, so there is nothing to install for basic guiding.

items.name: PHD2 (optional, the original app)
items.purpose: Prefer the real PHD2 over the native implementation? Install it on Windows or Linux, and Polaris drives it from inside the browser through an embedded remote view, no second screen needed. It still auto-detects PHD2, swaps profiles, runs Smart Calibrate, and broadcasts guide stats in real time.

items.name: Embedded remote view
items.purpose: Shows the installed PHD2 inside the Polaris GUIDE tab over a remote connection, no extra screen. Not supported on 32-bit Raspberry Pi (auto-gated).
items.windows: TightVNC, which Polaris bridges into the browser via noVNC.

optionalGroups.name: Post-processing
optionalGroups.intro: Detected at startup via the binary locator. Polaris grays out the matching STUDIO buttons when missing.

items.name: Siril
items.purpose: Replaces the built-in stacking pipeline in STUDIO with Siril scripts (5 bundled, plus your own ~/.siril/scripts).

items.name: GraXpert
items.purpose: Background extraction (auto per-frame during sequences if toggled), plus deconvolution and denoise on v3.0+.
items.linux: AppImage from the GraXpert releases page.

optionalGroups.name: Simulators (no hardware)
optionalGroups.intro: Test the whole pipeline without a scope. Settings then Equipment simulator detects the install and spawns the stack with one click.

items.name: INDI simulators
items.purpose: Renders real stars from the GSC catalog at the simulated mount position.
items.windows: Use the Alpaca Omni Simulator instead.

items.name: Alpaca Omni Simulator
items.purpose: A single .exe exposing the ASCOM Camera/Telescope/Focuser/FilterWheel simulators over Alpaca.
items.windows: Download and run the Omni Simulator.

items.name: Relay server (remote internet access)
items.purpose: Reach your rig from anywhere without exposing it directly. Reverse-tunnels over HTTPS with per-tenant tokens, mTLS, quotas, and built-in Let's Encrypt.
items.windows: Host NINA.Relay.Server on a public VPS (Linux). The rig side needs nothing extra.
items.linux: Run the Linux x64/arm64 build on a VPS with a domain and ports 80/443 open.

items.name: Remote terminal
items.purpose: Browser-based SSH from the Polaris tab to restart services on a headless host. Set Terminal:Enabled = true in appsettings.json.
items.linux: sudo apt install openssh-server (already present on Raspberry Pi OS).

items.name: Stellarium sync
items.purpose: Pull the currently selected object from Stellarium into the SKY tab as a target.
items.windows: Enable Plugins then Remote Control, bind to 127.0.0.1:8090.
items.linux: Same: enable the Remote Control plugin on 127.0.0.1:8090.
